extracted.intended_audience: nonprofit grantseekers / development staff applying for grants
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, post-decision steps for nonprofit grant applicants and development professionals to respond productively when a grant proposal is rejected, including seeking feedback, revising, and pursuing alternate funders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t take it personally
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They rejected your proposal, not you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call the funder for insight
rubrics_metrics.description: Call the funder to see if they can offer any insights on why the proposal was not funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the call to gather constructive information about weaknesses, fit, or priorities that led to the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request reviewer comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Request a copy of the reviewer’s comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain detailed reviewer feedback so you can identify specific deficiencies or misunderstandings to address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask about resubmission and strengthening
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask if you can resubmit in the next funding cycle and how you can strengthen your proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify eligibility for resubmission and solicit concrete suggestions for improvements to make your next application more competitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invite funder to visit programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Extend an invitation for them to tour your facility and see your programs in action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use site visits to build relationships, demonstrate impact, and address potential concerns reviewers may have had about feasibility or implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research the competition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn from the strengths of other proposals and try to apply that to your grant writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take copious notes of feedback
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep track of the feedback you have received so that you can reference this when your next proposal is due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Move on and re-prioritize funders
rubrics_metrics.description: Move on – go back to your potential funding matrix and select another proposal to knock out of the park!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a funding pipeline or matrix to prioritize alternate opportunities rather than dwelling on the rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get peer review (another set of eyes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask for another set of eyes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make sure you have someone else read your proposal to ask questions and strengthen the language from an outside perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hire a professional reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: Hire a professional to review your proposal before you press submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider paying an expert or consultant to critique and polish the application to improve competitiveness.
